title: Prototyping a horror game idea: my take on the "camera glitches" effect
author: Bill_Buffet
selftext:
I've been prototyping new game ideas lately, and one I keep coming back to is a found-footage horror game where you see everything through an old 90s camcorder.

I know I'm not the first to do this. Slender made the camera static when he's near you, Outlast has its camcorder, and a lot of indie horror uses glitchy video to show danger. So this isn't a new invention, just my approach to it.

What I'm trying to do differently is make the tape itself your health, instead of a temporary effect that comes and goes. The damage stays in the recording, and it breaks down in stages the way an old tape really would. A little damage and the picture warps and glitch bars roll through. More damage and the colour fades and noise creeps in. Near the end it fills with static and the picture starts rolling, like a dying VCR. The camcorder's battery icon in the corner doubles as your health. So the worse you're doing, the less you can see, and you have to play through that.

I also tried to make the camera feel like a real object rather than a filter: the autofocus hunts when something gets close, the auto-gain catches up a beat late when you turn, the cheap lens bends the edges, and you can switch to an infrared night mode.

It all runs in real time in a small engine I'm building, and I've been working on it together with Claude Code. The video shows how the different layers stack up and how the damage breaks the picture.
